Got it—no scary exposed hikes. I’ll steer your Zion plan toward low-exposure walks, such as the paved Pa’rus Trail along the Virgin River, and leave cliff-edge hikes out. [NPS: Pa’rus Trail](https://www.nps.gov/thingstodo/hike-pa-rus-trail.htm)

One date check before I build the four days: did you mean **September 12–17, 2027**? The 2026 dates we have have passed.

Absolutely—**no scary exposed hikes.** I’d keep your four Zion sightseeing days gentle, with river walks and viewpoints rather than cliff-edge routes.

These are deliberately relaxed days. I’d rather revisit a comfortable place than add a hike whose exposure I can’t verify. Times below are suggested time on site, not verified trail-completion times.

### Day 1 — Pa’rus: river scenery and Zion’s story
**Pa’rus Trail — 2 hours.** Take an unhurried out-and-back from the Zion Canyon Visitor Center, enjoying the Virgin River, Watchman views, and trailside exhibits about wildlife, geology, and human history. The entire trail is **1.6 miles each way**, but you needn’t complete it. Keep the **Pa’rus–Diversion Dam** viewpoint part of this outing rather than treating it as another hike. [NPS trail details](https://www.nps.gov/thingstodo/hike-pa-rus-trail.htm)

### Day 2 — Temple of Sinawava and evening light
- **Temple of Sinawava — 90 minutes.** Make this your main easy walking outing, with time to linger over the canyon scenery. This recommendation is for the Temple area—not an extension into a different trail or river hike.
- **Pa’rus Trail — 60 minutes near sunset.** Return specifically for evening Watchman views rather than another full trail walk. NPS identifies Pa’rus as a sunset outing. [NPS](https://www.nps.gov/thingstodo/hike-pa-rus-trail.htm)

### Day 3 — Lava Point’s different perspective
**Lava Point Overlook — 90 minutes.** Give this a separate, slow-paced scenic day: enjoy the overlook, landscape viewing, and a picnic rather than adding an unverified rim hike. It’s listed as easy and low-exposure, but **road access and opening status need checking before committing to the journey**. [NPS overlook information](https://www.nps.gov/places/lava-point-overlook.htm)

### Day 4 — A comfortable canyon finale
- **Temple of Sinawava — 75 minutes.** Revisit for another gentle walk and a final look at the canyon.
- **Pa’rus Trail — 90 minutes.** Finish with the river scenery and exhibits you most enjoyed or passed earlier. This is an intentional repeat, not a supposedly different hike under another name.

**For your exposure preference:** I’ve left out Big Bend and Canyon Junction as separate outings because I couldn’t verify their exposure. “Low exposure” also isn’t a guarantee that every spot will feel comfortable—stay on established routes and turn back whenever terrain feels wrong.

Current access isn’t confirmed for these places, so check NPS road, trail, and shuttle information before setting the order. This gives you **four gentle sightseeing days**, not four packed days of different hikes.
